column1: # Human-verified ingredients for products absent from RxNorm and openFDA.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS
# RxNorm and openFDA index US products. Several products in common Nigerian use
# are simply not in them — Alabukun
# Fansidar and others. build-catalog.ts EXCLUDES those rather than guessing
# because a product with a partial or invented ingredient list looks checkable
# and is not
column2: which is the exact failure that hurts someone.

column1: # This file is how they get back in: a human reads the actual pack and records
# what is printed on it.
# RULES
# 1. `verified_by` and `verified_at` are REQUIRED. A row without both is ignored
#    entirely
# 2. `ingredient_rxcui` must be the RxNorm ingredient code
#    check compares the same identity as the rest of the catalog. Look it up at
#    https://rxnav.nlm.nih.gov/REST/rxcui.json?name=<ingredient>&search=1
#    Paracetamol and acetaminophen are both 161 — that collapsing is the point.
# 3. `source` should say what was read: "pack
#    manufacturer datasheet URL. Not "known" and not a person's memory.
# 4. Record EVERY active ingredient on the pack. An incomplete row is worse than
#    no row
column2: because it re-introduces exactly the partial-list problem.
